key_insight: Machine-learned molecular dynamics predicts that approximately 0.5% biaxial tensile strain drives MAPbI₃ from tetragonal to cubic symmetry at 300 K while retaining preferential molecular orientations.
engineering_relevance: Finite-temperature strain modeling can guide epitaxial perovskite design by predicting phase stability and band-gap shifts that static calculations can miss.
method: Train machine-learned force fields on-the-fly using DFT.
Run nanosecond-scale bulk and free-standing slab simulations with fixed in-plane lattice vectors.
Track structural changes and average band gaps over MD snapshots.
evidence_signal: Bulk and slab simulations show consistent strain trends, with the predicted transition and tensile-strain band-gap blue shift agreeing with reported experiments.
watch_item: Free-standing slabs do not explicitly capture substrate-interface chemistry, which may affect transferability to specific epitaxial films.
paper_title: Strain-Induced Tetragonal-to-Cubic Transition in MAPbI$_3$ from Machine-Learned Molecular Dynamics
